conventions.convention: The parameter domain is P = {(m,a,q) ∈ R³ : m > 0, m² > a² + q²}, with zero magnetic flux and the selected SI parameter map. Extremal and zero-mass boundary points are excluded.

Geometric surface gravity uses the selected length-normalized horizon generator; κ_acc = c²κ_geom. Each fixed-member reduced branch uses that same generator and normalization, constant κ = κ_geom(x), a positive energy gap, and positive rate coefficient.

T_K(x) = ℏcκ_geom(x)/(2πk_B) is a reference-temperature function on the parameter family, not a local proper-temperature field. The reversible relation δQ_rev = T_K dS_H is an additional adopted physical assumption.
S_H is a C¹ state function measured in J/K; the heat relation is an equality of one-forms on the full parameter domain. No entropy reference value is imposed.
Countable Choice is explicitly retained as a mathematical premise of the supplier chains. The results are conditional model deductions with no empirical premises.
The two Schwarzschild states have positive SI masses and belong to the same connected calibrated family, so their entropy values share one additive constant.

load_bearing.statement: On P, adopt δQ_rev := dE_par − Ω_SI dJ_SI − Φ_SI dQ_e = T_K dS_H, with S_H a C¹ entropy state function and T_K(x) = ℏcκ_geom(x)/(2πk_B), using the explicitly matched fixed-member reduced branches and Countable Choice.

Under the stated strict-family, SI-map, Countable Choice, reversible-heat and pointwise reduced-temperature hypotheses, there is a constant s_* ∈ R, with units J/K, such that throughout P, S_H = k_B A_H/(4ℓ_P²) + s_* = k_B c³ A_H/(4G_Nℏ) + s_*, where ℓ_P² := G_Nℏ/c³.
